mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Parent Legal Entity (or equivalent registration proof)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies House / Registry of Companies in the jurisdiction of incorporation of the foreign shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If issued by a Hague Apostille Convention member state: obtain Apostille from the competent authority of the issuing state, then submit directly to the Chinese Notary Public for translation and notarization (no Chinese consular legalization). If issued by a non-member state: obtain notarization from the local notary, then legalization by the Chinese Embassy or Consulate in that jurisdiction; the legalized document must then be translated into Chinese by a certified translation agency in China and affixed with the seal of the notary public.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (or Certificate of Existence) of the Foreign Shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official corporate registry or competent government authority of the shareholder's home country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: issue Apostille from the competent authority of the shareholder's country (if member of the Hague Apostille Convention), then arrange notarized Chinese translation in China. Consular path for non-member states: notarization in the country of origin, then Chinese consular legalization, followed by notarized translation in China. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive and must never be combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney authorizing the formation of the China WFOE and designating the legal representative / manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors (or equivalent governing body) of the foreign investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille member state: Apostille by the designated competent authority, then notarized Chinese translation in China. Non-member state: notarization by local notary, Chinese consular legalization at China's embassy/consulate, then notarized translation in China. In either case, the resolution must clearly state the scope of authority, name of the designated person, and company formation details.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (or Constitutional Documents) of the foreign investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official registry where the foreign entity is incorporated
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille from the competent authority in the country of incorporation if a member of the Hague Apostille Convention, followed by notarized translation in China. Consular legalization (notarization + Chinese embassy/consulate legalization) if the country is not a member of the Apostille Convention. The documents must be complete and include any amendments; a certified copy must be used.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter (or Credit Reference Letter) for the foreign investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: A recognized commercial bank in the jurisdiction where the foreign investor maintains its primary banking relationship
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille from the competent authority of the bank's country if a Hague Apostille member, then notarized translation in China. Consular legalization if not a member. The letter must be issued within 30 days prior to submission and must be signed by an authorized bank officer, with contact details for verification.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Prior to incorporation and during the entire corporate life of the WFOE, the foreign investor and all ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) must be screened against the following lists: (1) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, (2) the U.S. Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) and Non-SDN lists, (3) the Consolidated Sanctions List of the European Union, (4) the List of Terrorists and terrorist organizations designated by the People's Republic of China per the Anti-Terrorism Law, (5) the front-page list of unusual and risky web platforms issued by the PBOC and the Ministry of Public Security, and (6) other sanctions lists administered by the People's Bank of China (PBOC) and the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR). Screening must be performed in real time at the time of onboarding and on an ongoing risk-based basis, at least quarterly, and must include name-matching algorithms that account for transliteration variations, aliases, date of birth, and national identification numbers. Foreign investors that are natural persons must undergo enhanced due diligence (EDD) if they are Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) as defined by the revised AML Law of 2024, including family members and close associates. The compliance team must document screening results with time-stamped audit trails, and any potential hit must be escalated to the AML compliance officer and cause a rejection of the beneficial owner unless a written clearance is obtained from the relevant regulator. The entire screening process must comply with the 'Know Your Customer' principles under PBOC Order No. 1 (2016) as amended, and must satisfy the record-keeping requirements of Article 17 of the 2024 AML Law.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Integrated Enterprise Registration and Filing System managed by the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) via the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (NECIPS; http://www.gsxt.gov.cn), with local counterpart portals operated by the Provincial Administration for Market Regulation where the WFOE is to be registered
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A WFOE's legal name in China must be composed in Chinese characters and follow the four-tier mandatory structure: (1) Administrative Division Name (city or province), (2) Distinguishing Name (chosen trade name), (3) Industry or Business Characteristic (e.g., 'E-commerce', 'Supply Chain'), and (4) Corporate Form ('Co., Ltd.'). The chosen name must not contain any characters that are contrary to the public interest, discriminatory, or misleadingly similar to an existing registered enterprise name. A corresponding English name may be used for foreign business operations but is not the registered legal name; it must not conflict with any trademarks or existing companies in China, and it must not contain any word that implies a scope beyond the approved business scope. Transliteration from the English trade name to Chinese characters is allowed as long as the pronunciation or meaning is acceptable to SAMR and does not violate naming prohibitions. Pinyin alone (without Chinese characters) cannot constitute the registered name, and the use of alphabetic characters is generally prohibited except for well-known acronyms only upon ministerial approval. Industry classifications for dropshipping must be stated as '互联网销售' or '跨境电商' or '自动售货机经营' depending on the actual business model; the name must accurately reflect the primary business category as defined in the Regulations on Enterprise Name Registration (State Council Decree No. 734, effective 2021).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name clearance application is rejected by the local Administration for Market Regulation (AMR), the applicant may file an administrative reconsideration (行政复议) with the same AMR or its superior authority within 60 calendar days from the date of the written rejection notice, pursuant to the Administrative Reconsideration Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Amendment). The appeal must be submitted in Chinese, accompanied by the original rejection notice, the identification of the applicant, and a memorandum explaining, with legal citations, why the proposed name should be approved. If the ADR rejects the proposed name on the ground of 'identical or similar' to an existing name in accordance with Article 6 of the Provisions on the Registration of Enterprise Names (SAMR Order No. 42, 2020), the appellant must obtain from the existing registrant a formal written consent (名称使用同意函) or propose a modified name that is sufficiently distinct. If the reconsideration is denied, the applicant may further file an administrative lawsuit within 15 days from the service of the reconsideration decision in the People's Court, per Articles 39 and 40 of the Administrative Litigation Law. The entire rejection and appeal process typically takes 15–30 days; the applicant may, during the reconsideration, simultaneously apply for a new name reservation using an alternative name with different distinguishing elements. It is critical to note that the name reservation is not tied to any particular entity identification number; therefore, the appellant can preserve the appeal rights while restarting a new name search. The local AMR must issue a written decision within 30 days of accepting the reconsideration petition. During the appeal, the applicant should proactively supply the original name screening results and the full list of similar registered names to demonstrate that the proposed name does not cause confusion among the public.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is not permitted for a WFOE engaged in automated dropshipping, unless the virtual office provider offers a lawful, non-residential business license in the jurisdiction of registration and an actual physical premises subject to inspection. Under the Regulations on the Control of Enterprise Registration (State Council Decree No. 746, 2021), all enterprises must have a registered address that can accept legal process, and the address must be consistent with the place of business operations as declared to tax authorities and customs. For cross-border e-commerce and dropshipping activities, the State Administration of Taxation (SAT) and the local tax bureaus require a physical office that can produce, upon request, complete records of purchase orders, sales orders, logistics receipts, and banking transactions. Further, the Payment Management Rules (PBOC Order No. 1, 2010) and the AML Rules require banks and payment service providers to perform physical verification of the registered business location before opening a merchant account; therefore, a mailbox-only address is rejected by all major commercial banks and payment gateway providers (such as Stripe and PayPal) when underwriting cross-border merchants. In practice, a WFOE must maintain a residential-quality leased office space (面积) of at least 10 square meters, with a desk, a dedicated telephone line, a physical sign, and fire-safety compliance certificates. The virtual office may be used only as an ancillary administrative support, never as the sole registered address. The risk of rejection by tax authorities is high if the address appears on a list of high-incidence virtual office registrations, and the entity may be designated as 'address abnormal' (地址异常), leading to a freeze of its tax invoice quota and inclusion in the list of enterprises with abnormal conditions, which blocks further name changes, share transfers, and termination of social insurance account.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Unannounced physical on-site inspections are conducted by the local Administration for Market Regulation (AMR), the State Taxation Administration (local tax bureau), and the Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) for foreign-funded enterprises, particularly those in the cross-border e-commerce sector. Based on current enforcement patterns, the likelihood of at least one inspection within the first 12 months is estimated to be 35%–50% for a newly established WFOE in the online retail sector, and the likelihood rises to 70% if the entity has been flagged for any non-compliance indication (e.g., invoicing anomaly, abnormally high turnover relative to office size, or failure to provide an up-to-date copy of the lease). The inspection checklist includes: (1) verification that the registration address is actually occupied and used by the company; (2) checking the company name sign is properly affixed; (3) confirming the legal representative and manager are present on site or have a designated deputy; (4) inspecting the availability of original charters, business license, and financial accounting records; (5) verifying that the number of employees matches the declared social insurance payroll; (6) reviewing the physical inventory and orders if any goods are stored; (7) examining the server logs and computing equipment for automated trading systems; and (8) ensuring that any cross-border payment systems (Stripe, PayPal) are integrated with a compliant local settlement bank account. A no-notice inspection can be triggered by an anonymous complaint, a bank suspicion report (STR), or a random draw from a unified platform (e.g., the 'double random, one open' inspection mechanism introduced by the General Office of the State Council). The quantitative risk factor for a low-office-usage scenario is 0.85 on a 0–1 scale; i.e., 85% chance that an inspection occurring without prior warning will result in an administrative order for correction, potentially leading to a fine of up to 30% of the enterprise's illegal gains or RMB 100,000 if the entity is deemed as providing false registration information. To mitigate this risk, the WFOE must maintain at least one part-time office staff member with a written labor contract and trim the physical premises with a functioning work area, and must respond to any inspection within 24 hours with a complete statutory file.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: State-imposed Advertising Fee / Public Disclosure of UBO (Beneficial Owner Information Filing Fee)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Under Order No. 3 (2024), the submission of beneficial owner information to the SAMR system and the PBOC registry is free of charge; no filing fee is authorized.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and Apostille / Consular Legalization of the foreign shareholder's corporate documents (per set, including Certificate of Incorporation, Good Standing, Board Resolution, Articles, and Bank Reference Letter)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Foreign notary public, competent authority for Apostille (e.g., US Secretary of State / UK Foreign Office), and the Chinese Embassy or Consulate in the respective jurisdiction
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing international market benchmark: USD 150 to USD 400 per document bundle depending on the country; includes apostille fees (USD 15–40 per document) and notary fees; consular legalization fees follow the published tariff of the Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs (approximately USD 30–80 per document).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified Chinese Translation and Notarization of Apostilled/Consularized Foreign Documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registered translation agency and a Chinese Notary Public (公证处)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market rate for contract translation in China is RMB 200–400 per 1,000 Chinese characters (USD 30–60), plus notarial certification fee of RMB 100–400 per document (USD 15–60). The budget covers one bundle of translated and notarized documents (approximately 1,500 characters).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Trusted Name Clearance and Pre-appraisal Service by an AML/CFT-licensed local law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: The engaging law firm (no government component)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Customary fixed fee for name clearance and compliance pre-screening in first-tier cities range from USD 80 to USD 250; flat fee of USD 120 incorporates the SAMR name check, similarity search, and preliminary review of the four-tier naming convention.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Official Publication and Publicity Fee (if required by the local AMR for foreign-owned enterprises)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Local AMR or the designated government gazette platform
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fully waived after the 2020 enterprise registration reform; no publication fee is charged for initial establishment; only a voluntary announcement fee may apply if the enterprise chooses to make an additional public notice, which is not required by law.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Lease Agreement Registration and Stamp Duty (Tax on the Commercial Office Lease for the WFOE's registered address)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Local tax bureau (under the State Taxation Administration) and the real estate leasing registration authority
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Stamp duty at 0.1% of the total annual rental value (local tax regulations vary from 0.05% to 0.1%); for a minimum office of RMB 6,000/year (approx. USD 850), the duty is USD 0.85, but the registration fee, contract template, and notarization of the lease certificate add USD 50–100; enterprises typically pay USD 200–300 to a legal agent to facilitate the registration. The USD 250 estimate covers stamp duty, lease registration, and facilitating services.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Trademark Search for the WFOE's Distinguishing Name (Optional but Recommended)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: China National Intellectual Property Administration (CNIPA) trademark database via a certified agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: CNIPA official search is free; the fee is for an attorney-driven freedom-to-operate search and similarity analysis to ensure the company name may later be used as a trademark. Market rate is USD 60–150 per class combination.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 revision, effective 1 July 2024), Articles 13, 23, 24, 27, 29, 31, 33, 46, 47 and 50; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2020), Articles 2, 3, 6, 8 and 22; Implementing Regulations of the Foreign Investment Law (2020), Articles 11 through 14; and Company Registration Administrative Regulations of the People's Republic of China.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and the municipal or provincial Market Supervision Administration located in the city of the company's registered office.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Foreign-Invested Enterprise Establishment Registration Application Form (Company Business License Registration) and the accompanying Foreign Investment Information Report.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to an ordinary wholly foreign-owned enterprise in the permitted e-commerce and automated dropshipping sector. The Articles of Association must state registered capital and a lawful contribution schedule; capital may be contributed in full or in installments as agreed. No blocked escrow account is required by the Company Law, but all inbound capital from the foreign investor must be remitted through a Chinese bank under SAFE capital-account rules and the proceeds must be applied to the company's declared business purposes. Where cross-border payments to dropshipping suppliers use the capital account, the bank must receive the FDI registration form and underlying transaction evidence.

SECOND: THE TOTAL REGISTERED CAPITAL OF THE COMPANY SHALL BE THE AMOUNT STATED IN THE ARTICLES, AND THE SOLE SHAREHOLDER IS HEREBY AUTHORIZED TO SUBSCRIBE FOR ALL ISSUED SHARES; CONTRIBUTIONS SHALL BE MADE IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE CONTRIBUTION SCHEDULE, AND NO BLOCKED ESCROW ACCOUNT IS REQUIRED. THIRD: THE DIRECTORS ARE AUTHORIZED TO OPEN RMB AND FOREIGN EXCHANGE BANK ACCOUNTS AT A COMMERCIAL BANK SELECTED BY THE CHIEF FINANCIAL OFFICER, AND TO DESIGNATE THE GENERAL MANAGER AND CHIEF FINANCIAL OFFICER AS JOINT SIGNATORIES FOR ALL ACCOUNT OPERATIONS. FOURTH: THE REGISTERED OFFICE OF THE COMPANY SHALL BE [ADDRESS], AND THE LEGAL REPRESENTATIVE IS AUTHORIZED TO EXECUTE THE LEASE AGREEMENT AND FILE THE REGISTERED OFFICE WITH THE REGISTRY.
